assumptions.summary: Minimize the number of expensive drones so that the ISO containers can carry more medical packages.
Treat the drones as reusable rather than disposable and require replaceable batteries after deployment.
Reserve about three to four hours between operations for battery replacement.
Prohibit night work and limit each UAV to at most three operations per day.
Exclude type H from medical delivery and road reconnaissance, but place one tethered H drone in every container for communications.
Keep medical packages in their permitted upright transport orientation inside ISO containers while allowing horizontal rotation.
Allow more package orientations inside a drone cargo bay because each flight carries fewer items for less time.
Set maximum loaded flight time to two thirds of unloaded flight time.
Keep maximum speed unchanged when converting loaded endurance to range.
Charge one minute of flight time for ascent and descent, without a separate climb or descent profile.
Require each delivered package bundle to be an integer multiple of the target hospital's daily demand.

contributions.summary: Compresses fleet, ISO packing, road gridding, siting, cargo-bay packing, delivery routing, reconnaissance routing, and scheduling into one Summary pipeline.
States an explicit priority order: satisfy daily hospital demand, extend support duration, reduce UAV count, and then expand reconnaissance.
Screens spatial isolation and shared-hospital feasibility before selecting drone types and assigning container territories.
Uses a package-first and UAV-later packing narrative intended to remain understandable during physical loading.
Creates one grid interface that connects road coverage, hospital reach, site selection, delivery paths, and reconnaissance tours.
Makes package bundles operational by connecting support days to delivery frequency and available reconnaissance time.
Separates obstacle-rich and obstacle-light routing cases before constructing explicit waypoint paths.
Turns routes and payload assignments into delivery-only and combined three-day operating calendars.
Prints partial implementations for gridding, packing, siting, Voronoi geometry, ACO, and route drawing, creating a useful but incomplete replay surface.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Use the official Puerto Rico hurricane scenario, five hospitals, daily package demand, eight lettered drone types including tethered H, two cargo-bay types, three medical-package types, and a three-container cap.
Read five hospital locations and demand assignments from Attachment 4 before screening shared-service possibilities.
Use attachment drone shipping dimensions, payload, speed, unloaded endurance, video capability, medical capability, and cargo-bay type in the weighted type-selection step.
Assign each candidate fleet scheme to three containers, hospital territories, and required MED1, MED2, and MED3 families.
Use ISO interior dimensions, drone shipping-container dimensions, and medical-package dimensions in the ODMU volume and residual calculations.
Substitute the attachment dimensions into the constructive packing equations to obtain package counts, medical volume, UAV volume, and utilization.
Convert a Puerto Rico main-road raster into a binary grid whose TG cells indicate road presence.
Use a reported 113.99 km horizontal extent and 91 cells to define grid scale, then map the five hospitals to (15,92), (25,61), (6,57), (11,51), and (4,4).
Use selected drone half-ranges, hospital assignments, and binary road cells to search candidate container locations.
Use the two cargo-bay geometries, package dimensions and masses, daily demand, and drone maximum payload to construct sortie bundles.
Represent nearby mountains and tall buildings as threat points for the container-2 route region.
Use Voronoi intersections, hospitals, container sites, and unspecified graph distances as the Dijkstra delivery network.
Use selected TG nodes and pairwise distances as the TSP and ant-colony interfaces for reconnaissance.
The grid.m listing reads the missing The path.jpg image, thresholds its green channel at 200, and coarsens it with precision 5.
The cargo.m listing reads the missing T.xlsx file, sets S=113.990 and n=91, converts Sd=39.5/2 to grid radius, and searches hard-coded candidate bounds.
The Vd.m listing supplies ten threat coordinates for one Voronoi plot.
The Q4.m listing declares C, NC_max, m, Alpha, Beta, Rho, and Q as inputs, but the report supplies no calls, parameter values, coordinate matrices, or random seed.

dependency_graph.summary: Shared-service feasibility and isolated-hospital structure define the assignments for drone-type selection.
The two candidate fleet structures are decomposed into three container service territories.
Selected drone letters and multiplicities populate the two candidate container schemes.
Each scheme's drone and package families define the required items for initial package filling.
The package-filled layout and residual spaces become the preimage for UAV insertion.
Orientation-specific removal counts produce the two reported packing result tables.
Both candidate service schemes are tested for common hospital-reach feasibility during siting.
Binary road cells, grid scale, and mapped hospitals supply the siting objective and constraints.
Scheme-2 site infeasibility resolves the earlier fleet-scheme choice in favour of the retained scheme.
Selected sites and hospital assignments determine service frequency and required payload bundles.
Drone types provide cargo-bay geometry and maximum payload for bundle design.
Container and hospital grid coordinates locate the endpoints around which obstacle corridors are built.
The Voronoi skeleton becomes the candidate graph for Dijkstra delivery paths.
Delivery paths and distances supply travel times for the three-day timetable.
Payload support days determine which hospitals require service on each day.
Unused mission windows and container origins constrain the reconnaissance tour problem.
Road-grid points inside each site region become candidate reconnaissance nodes.
The TSP node and distance interfaces are passed to stochastic ant-tour construction.
Completed ant tours and lengths supply pheromone deposits and best-tour updates.
Selected reconnaissance tours are interleaved with delivery to form the overall three-day schedule.
Reported delivery paths are converted to lengths and checked against assigned maximum range.
Reported reconnaissance tours are converted to lengths and checked against assigned maximum range.
The grid.m implementation is the claimed source of the binary road-cell interface.
The packing.m and ISO.m residual arithmetic partially implements the ODMU planar fill.
The cargo.m finite search partially implements road-cell coverage maximization.
The Vd.m coordinate list supplies threat points for the Voronoi diagram.
Q4.m implements ACO tour construction and exposes the stochastic search state.
Q4.m implements pheromone update, best-tour retention, and trace plotting.

independent_extensions.summary: Solve fleet, facility, inventory, and time-indexed sortie decisions jointly with explicit demand, energy, batteries, crews, and certified bounds.
Replace one-axis ODMU arithmetic with a mass-aware three-dimensional packing and loading model that supplies coordinates, orientations, access, support, and replay files.
Build a georeferenced road graph with unique-segment coverage, obstacle polygons, clearance buffers, wind, altitude, camera footprint, and route-executable inspection value.
Calibrate payload-energy curves and validate routes, schedules, and road-damage detection with repeated simulations and independent field or benchmark outcomes.
Publish a complete environment with frozen inputs, Dijkstra and ACO implementations, parameters, seeds, exact small-instance comparators, output manifests, and uncertainty traces.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge may value the Summary's direct task-method-result ladder across every requested operational deliverable, while all broad performance language remains conditional.
A judge may value that the memorandum converts sites, fleets, routes, schedules, road coverage, and battery choices into explicit HELP-facing recommendations.
A judge may value the grid as a shared interface from geography to coverage, delivery, and reconnaissance, provided that scale and topology are corrected and replayed.
A judge may value the unusually extensive code appendix as evidence of implementation effort, while recognizing that it is not a complete executable package.

language_observations.summary: task-method-result ladder: Compress a many-part operational response by pairing each required task with its method, reported output, and next handoff.
finding-consequence-recommendation chain: Translate model outputs into executive advice by naming the finding, operational consequence, recommendation, and condition for changing course.
requirement decomposition and handoff: Turn a broad prompt into ordered work packages whose outputs become typed inputs to later decisions.
premise-rationale-consequence boundary: State a simplification, explain why it is introduced, identify the affected mechanism, and preserve the downstream validity boundary.
definition-constraint-output handoff: Introduce indexed quantities, state objectives and constraints, interpret the feasible output, and pass it to a later model.
state-test-update-stop algorithm narration: Expose a constructive or heuristic procedure through state, candidate action, feasibility test, update, stopping rule, and returned artifact.
visual-result-decision interpretation: Move from a named table, map, or diagram through a metric and comparison to a bounded operational decision.
check-threshold-claim boundary: Name the quantity checked, the admissible threshold, the observed comparison, the local conclusion, and what remains untested.
limitation-consequence-repair handoff: Name a source or reproducibility boundary, explain its decision consequence, and identify the missing data, test, or model extension.

models.summary: MU-B-2019-1924588-001: Identify whether one UAV can serve two hospitals and use spatial isolation to derive the minimum structural fleet count.
MU-B-2019-1924588-002: Score candidate UAV types by shipping volume, payload, and range while enforcing hospital demand and inter-hospital reach.
MU-B-2019-1924588-003: Assign candidate drone types, medical package families, and hospitals to three containers under spatial separation and support-duration reasoning.
MU-B-2019-1924588-004: Fill ISO containers with one package or daily-ratio bundles by minimizing an edge residual and stacking equal-height layers before UAV insertion.
MU-B-2019-1924588-005: Remove the fewest packages from residual-space-adjacent positions so that a required UAV shipping container fits in one of two planar orientations.
MU-B-2019-1924588-006: Compare two reported three-container layouts by package counts, UAV volumes, medical volumes, and spatial utilization, then prefer realizability over some utilization.
MU-B-2019-1924588-007: Convert the main-road image into binary road cells, define kilometres per cell, and map five hospitals into one grid coordinate system.
MU-B-2019-1924588-008: Choose three grid sites that cover many road cells inside a half-range circle while keeping assigned hospitals within the corresponding UAV half-range.
MU-B-2019-1924588-009: Pack integral daily-demand bundles into each selected drone cargo bay subject to geometric and payload limits.
MU-B-2019-1924588-010: Use obstacle points as threat sources and Voronoi edges as candidate low-threat corridors for the complex delivery region.
MU-B-2019-1924588-011: Find shortest paths on the Voronoi-derived node graph and connect off-skeleton container and hospital endpoints.
MU-B-2019-1924588-012: Assign delivery departures and returns over a repeating three-day cycle using the selected fleet, routes, payload bundles, and turnaround premise.
MU-B-2019-1924588-013: Find a minimum-distance closed tour from each container through selected road-grid points inside its reconnaissance range.
MU-B-2019-1924588-014: Sample the next unvisited reconnaissance node from pheromone and inverse-distance desirability.
MU-B-2019-1924588-015: Evaporate existing pheromone, add deposits from completed ant tours, and stop after a maximum cycle count.
MU-B-2019-1924588-016: Compare assigned delivery and reconnaissance route lengths with each UAV maximum flight distance.
MU-B-2019-1924588-017: Read a road image, threshold one colour channel, and aggregate pixels into a coarse binary grid used by coverage and routing.
MU-B-2019-1924588-018: Enumerate MED1 length-width combinations and retain the row with the largest reported capacity for one container direction.
MU-B-2019-1924588-019: Read a road-cell matrix, convert range to grid radius, loop over a bounded candidate rectangle, and retain the largest summed road value.
MU-B-2019-1924588-020: Supply a fixed coordinate array for constructing the obstacle Voronoi diagram around the complex delivery region.
MU-B-2019-1924588-021: Construct pairwise Euclidean distances, sample tabu tours, update pheromone, retain best and average lengths, and draw the selected tour.

results_trace.summary: The Summary reports candidate fleet 1 as one B, one C, one D, and three H drones, and candidate fleet 2 as two B, one C, one G, and three H drones.
The Summary reports packing utilization from 68.14 percent to 93.22 percent.
The Summary reports three geographic container sites near (18.47,-66.55), (18.34,-66.03), and (18.34,-65.69).
Section 4.1.2 prints two fleet options, but its second option names C, D, two B, and three H drones rather than the Summary's G-containing option.
Tables 2 and 3 assign three hospital territories, drone families, and medical-package families for two candidate schemes.
The first packing table reports container utilizations 93.22, 68.14, and 86.38 percent with UAV rows B+H, G+H, and B+C+H.
The continued second packing table reports container utilizations 93.22, 74.38, and 87 percent with UAV rows B+H, C+H, and D+H.
The grid search rejects scheme 2 and selects scheme 1 with grid sites (4,19), (15,61), and (15,89).
The selected grid sites are transformed to (18.47,-66.5459), (18.339,-66.0305), and (18.339,-65.6868).
Figure 10 reports one bundle for B, three alternatives for D, and three C assignments for hospitals II, III, and IV.
Table 7 reports five delivery waypoint sequences from the three selected container sites to hospitals I through V.
Table 8 reports delivery departures and returns over a three-day cycle with later C sorties at 12:30 and 16:30.
ACO produces one B reconnaissance route, two D routes, and three C routes in grid coordinates.
The overall operating table interleaves delivery and reconnaissance missions over a repeating three-day cycle.
The inspection table lists maximum ranges, delivery distances, and reconnaissance distances for F1, F2, and F3.
The paper concludes that every printed route stays within the assigned maximum range and calls the model reasonable.
The source credits ODMU utilization, grid measurability, multi-factor scope, and lower cost.
The source acknowledges incomplete road coverage and the absence of an exact loaded-flight-distance formula.

source_quality.notes: All 33 physical PDF pages were read in order and visually reviewed through seven byte-bounded full-page coverage proxies plus one focused packing-table crop. The eight proxies total 2832549 bytes and the largest is 449543 bytes. Complete page-aware extraction contains 43600 non-whitespace characters and 8867 words. Text preserves prose, labels, most formulas, tables, routes, references, and seven MATLAB appendix pages, but flattens radicals, floor marks, matrices, cases, arrows, subscripts, superscripts, table columns, and code indentation. Fleet, scheme, table, scale, formula, unit, route-closure, schedule, implementation, and claim conflicts remain explicit G7 warnings rather than silent repairs.

weaknesses.summary: The objective weights, normalization, sign convention for shipping volume, candidate scores, and sensitivity are absent, so the selected type cannot be replayed.
Section 4.1.2 names D in the second fleet, while the Summary, Figure 3, and Tables 2-3 imply a G-containing alternative; the report never reconciles the fleet identity.
The Summary, Figure 3, section 4.1.2, Tables 2-3, and the packing tables do not preserve one stable mapping from scheme number to drone inventory and hospital territory.
The first result table is called scheme 1 but its G-containing UAV row matches the earlier scheme-2 assignment.
The second result table is introduced as scheme 2 but its B-C-D UAV row matches the earlier scheme-1 assignment.
Both packing result tables are captioned Table 4 ISO container scheme 1, while the following prose refers to tables 4 and 5.
Large package counts and utilization percentages do not by themselves establish hospital-specific support duration, inventory balance, package mass, accessibility, or long-term service.
113.99 km divided by 91 cells is about 1.2526 km per cell, not the printed 1.281 km per cell; every transformed distance needs recomputation.
The printed S relation is a sum of squared coordinate differences without a square root, conflicting with its earlier use as distance and leaving the half-range constraint dimensionally ambiguous.
The floor-plus-one rule can remove an extra layer when the required clearance is an exact multiple and has no max-with-zero guard when residual space already suffices.
Equations (9)-(12) use alternative divisors and residual dimensions without a complete orientation rule, coordinate placement, or collision proof.
Multiplying three one-axis removal counts does not prove that exactly that many occupied cuboids must be removed or that the UAV can be inserted without collision.
Volume, one-axis residuals, and equal-height layers do not prove full three-dimensional nonoverlap, weight feasibility, load bearing, access, balance, buffer needs, or optimality.
The index structure is ambiguous and summed dimensions are not a complete three-dimensional packing or centre-of-gravity formulation.
The shown cargo.m implementation sums a clipped square window, not visibly the circular objective in equation (14), and does not visibly enforce every hospital constraint or all three site searches.
Equidistance along a point-site Voronoi edge does not prove adequate clearance from all obstacle geometry, terrain, buildings, wind, or no-fly constraints.
The report omits the Dijkstra implementation, graph adjacency, edge weights, endpoint-connector rule, tie policy, and route-distance replay.
The required adjustment from off-skeleton container and hospital endpoints is unspecified and may invalidate both shortest-distance and safety claims.
Table 8 is captioned as a reconnaissance video schedule even though the text says it contains only medical-delivery timing.
The timetable does not model exact speed, loading, unloading, batteries, charging, crews, simultaneous resources, maintenance, demand arrival, no-night boundaries, or reserve energy.
The report does not define how selected TG points represent all required road segments, so a shortest node tour need not maximize useful or unique road reconnaissance.
The prose uses tau_k for the visited-node record even though tau denotes pheromone elsewhere, and the admissible-set notation and normalization are not made implementation-stable.
ACO Step 4 sends an incomplete tour back to Step 2, which increments the cycle counter, instead of clearly continuing within-tour node selection.
The update timing t+N, evaporation semantics, parameters, initial pheromone, cycle budget, seed, repeated runs, convergence trace, runtime, and exact comparator are unreported.
Route 4 starts at (15,61) but ends at (15,60), violating the stated requirement that every reconnaissance mission return to its container.
The prose calls the overall schedule table 10 while its caption says Table 9, and calls the inspection table 11 while its caption says Table 10.
The printed 11.518m and 26.974m reconnaissance distances are inconsistent with the surrounding kilometre units and are likely unit-label errors that require source calculation replay.

Checking only route length against a nominal maximum cannot support perfect, reasonable, safe, or overall-feasible claims without payload, wind, reserve, altitude, timing, uncertainty, and independent outcome tests.
Loaded endurance is fixed at two thirds of unloaded endurance, while the source's own Weakness section admits that the exact loaded maximum-distance formula was not solved.

The appendix lacks The path.jpg, T.xlsx, input coordinate matrices, function calls, ACO parameters, random seed, Dijkstra code, complete result mapping, software version, and an executable environment.
The source acknowledges that minimizing fleet cost leaves some roads unreconnoitred.
The source acknowledges that exact maximum loaded-flight-distance behavior was not solved.
The appendix ends without the input image, spreadsheet, driver calls, Dijkstra implementation, frozen parameters, seed, environment, or a result manifest.

memo: HELP executive decision -> translate calculations into findings and recommendations -> connect reusable drones, three containers, selected sites, routes, schedules, and coverage tradeoffs to explicit actions -> stakeholder-facing deployment advice -> introduction

introduction: hurricane damage and official task clauses -> move from disaster consequences to six inspectable work packages and prior packing methods -> connect damaged infrastructure and medical demand to fleet, container, siting, payload, route, schedule, and reconnaissance deliverables -> problem architecture and literature boundary -> assumptions

assumptions: cost, battery, communication, handling, and flight uncertainties -> declare the simplified operating world -> bound fleet count, reuse, duty cycle, tethered communication, package orientation, loaded endurance, vertical time, and demand multiples -> conditional premise ledger -> notation and objective priorities

notation-objectives: typed symbols and competing priorities -> define a compact interface and a lexicographic decision order -> separate hospital distance, demand mass, drone range and load, dimensions, road cells, grid scale, site coordinates, hospital service, support duration, fleet cost, and video coverage -> symbol ledger and priority hierarchy -> fleet selection

fleet-selection: five hospitals, demands, drone specifications, and three-container limit -> derive two candidate fleet and service schemes -> isolate Arecibo, test shared-service feasibility, score drone types, choose three containers, and assign hospitals and package types -> two candidate fleets and container roles -> container packing method

container-packing-method: three candidate container assignments and item dimensions -> replace a generic NP-hard heuristic with a reproducible constructive narrative -> define sets and volumes, bundle package ratios, minimize one-axis residuals, stack layers, and remove the fewest packages for UAV placement -> ODMU packing procedure and removal equations -> packing results

container-packing-results: ODMU and two candidate fleet assignments -> turn packing arithmetic into an operational comparison -> report package counts, UAV contents, volumes, utilization, and the convenience-efficiency tradeoff for both schemes -> two quantified container configurations -> location optimization

location-model: selected fleet schemes, hospital service, and Puerto Rico road raster -> select three sites that preserve delivery while expanding road coverage -> grid roads, transform coordinates, map hospitals, maximize covered TG cells under half-range service constraints, and reject an infeasible scheme -> three selected container coordinates -> payload packing

payload-packing: daily hospital demand, drone bay geometry, and payload limits -> translate service frequency into inspectable cargo bundles -> require at least one day of demand, permit multi-day bundles, constrain orientations and mass, and report per-drone layouts -> drone-specific package configurations -> delivery routes

delivery-route: selected sites, hospitals, obstacle points, and payload assignments -> construct obstacle-aware delivery paths -> separate threat-rich and threat-light cases, build a Voronoi safety skeleton, apply Dijkstra, adjust off-skeleton endpoints, and report all five routes -> grid-coordinate delivery route set -> delivery schedule

delivery-schedule: route lengths, fleet, package bundles, duty-cycle assumptions, and hospital frequency -> convert paths into a repeating operating calendar -> assign departures and returns across three days while reserving reconnaissance work for the combined schedule -> three-day delivery timetable -> reconnaissance formulation

reconnaissance-formulation: TG nodes near each container and available mission windows -> turn road inspection into a closed-tour optimization -> define nodes, distances, binary arcs, degree constraints, subtour elimination, and minimum total distance within the reconnaissance region -> TSP-style route model -> ACO solution

aco-solution: the finite TSP node sets and pairwise distance matrix -> explain a heuristic search and translate tours into a combined schedule -> initialize ants and pheromones, sample transitions, update deposits, stop at a cycle cap, report six routes, and interleave them with delivery -> reconnaissance routes and overall timetable -> testing

testing: all delivery and reconnaissance route lengths -> perform a deterministic range check -> compare every reported route distance with the assigned UAV maximum and infer only route-length feasibility -> range-feasibility table -> evaluation

evaluation: the full internally generated solution -> summarize source-authored strengths and weaknesses -> credit packing, gridding, multi-factor scope, and cost while admitting incomplete road coverage and assumed loaded range -> bounded self-evaluation -> references

references: ten cited sources -> identify provenance roles without inflating them into supplied data -> separate packing algorithms, cellular-network context, disaster communication, trajectory planning, storage assignment, and drone-platform sources -> reference ledger and source gaps -> appendix
